security_audit.summary: All 130 static findings are false positives caused by documentation, Docker templates, internal health checks, defensive ignore rules, and readable helper-script constructs. The helper script includes an explicit destructive cleanup operation that can remove unused local Docker resources when a user invokes it. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, hidden execution, or malicious network behavior was found.

remediation.issue: The cleanup command force-removes unused Docker containers, images, volumes, and networks.
remediation.suggestion: Show the resources that would be removed and require an explicit confirmation flag before running prune commands. Document that unused volumes may contain recoverable data.

semantic_findings.title: Destructive Docker cleanup operation
semantic_findings.description: The helper script removes stopped containers, dangling images, unused volumes, and unused networks without a confirmation prompt. Running the cleanup command can delete local resources needed for recovery.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cleanup function directly invokes four Docker prune commands with force flags. This behavior is explicit and can remove user data or local state.

content.value_statement: Container setup can be inconsistent across development and production environments. This skill provides Dockerfile, Compose, debugging, and optimization guidance with reusable examples.
actual_capabilities: Creates multi-stage Dockerfile guidance for Node.js, Python, Go, Java, and Rust applications.
Explains Docker Compose service orchestration, health checks, networks, and persistent volumes.
Provides a comprehensive .dockerignore template for reducing build context and excluding sensitive files.
Offers Docker commands for inspecting containers, logs, ports, networks, and image layers.
Suggests image-size optimization techniques and production container practices.
limitations: It does not run Docker commands or deploy containers without user approval.
Examples use placeholder credentials and require secure values for real environments.
The helper script can affect local Docker resources and requires review before use.
It does not replace application-specific security, networking, or production testing.

use_cases.title: Containerize a new service
use_cases.description: Create a practical Dockerfile and Compose starting point for a local application.

use_cases.title: Improve a delivery image
use_cases.description: Review a Dockerfile for multi-stage builds, smaller images, and safer build context.

use_cases.title: Investigate a running container
use_cases.description: Use documented inspection steps to check logs, health, ports, processes, and networks.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Dockerfile
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a simple multi-stage Dockerfile for my application. Ask for its language, build command, runtime command, and exposed port.

prompt_templates.title: Add local services
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Docker Compose plan for my API, database, and cache. Include health checks, named volumes, and environment variable placeholders.

prompt_templates.title: Debug a container
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me diagnose a container that exits after startup. Give safe inspection commands for logs, configuration, health, and port mappings.

prompt_templates.title: Harden a release image
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Dockerfile for production readiness. Focus on non-root execution, minimal runtime dependencies, build context, image size, and secret handling.

output_examples.input: I need a Docker setup for a Python API with PostgreSQL.
output: A multi-stage build outline for the API.
A Compose service plan with PostgreSQL, health checks, and a named volume.
A list of environment variables to define outside version control.

output_examples.input: My Docker image is too large.
output: A prioritized list of image-size checks.
Recommendations for multi-stage builds and smaller base images.
Commands to inspect layers and validate the reduced image.

output_examples.input: A container is unhealthy after deployment.
output: A safe diagnostic sequence for status, logs, and health checks.

best_practices: Pin base-image versions and review their update policy.
Keep secrets outside Dockerfiles, Compose files, image layers, and version control.
Review destructive Docker commands and verify their scope before running them.
anti_patterns: Do not use development passwords or default secrets in production.
Do not copy broad project directories into images without a .dockerignore file.
Do not run cleanup commands when you need unused volumes or images for recovery.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: It supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does this skill deploy my application?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. You control all Docker and deployment commands.

faq.question: Does it include Compose examples?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers service orchestration, health checks, networks, volumes, queues, and monitoring examples.

faq.question: How should I handle secrets?
faq.answer: Use environment management or a secret manager. Do not embed secrets in images or committed Compose files.

faq.question: Is the helper script safe to run?
faq.answer: Review its command and arguments first. Its cleanup operation removes unused local Docker resources.

faq.question: Can I use the templates in production?
faq.answer: Use them as a starting point, then adapt image versions, credentials, networking, observability, and security controls.
